canonicalBase.reason: Preserves the current Prisma backend, Supabase migrations, Docker/deployment files, security scanning, and CI surface while reconciliation proceeds slice by slice.

authorityRules: Postgres is canonical for shared ChopDot operational state.
Polkadot is canonical only for facts that actually occur on-chain.
Client storage is limited to drafts, cache, and explicitly local-only state.
A payment request is not a payment.
Payer evidence moves a settlement to paid or marked_paid; receiver confirmation closes manual settlement under the current policy.
Private keys and seed material never enter ChopDot.

workflowContracts.rule: A capability-gated workflow must name missing assets and must never describe a blocked run as test or release evidence.

portOrder: RECONCILIATION-000: establish protected authoritative baseline and executable CI
DATA-002: integer canonical money and versioned persistence migrations
BACKEND-001: authenticated and idempotent command service
BACKEND-002: durable obligations, payment intents, settlement evidence, and audit events
PRODUCT-SLICES: port stronger money, people, group, history, identity, Polkadot, and accessibility work one bounded slice at a time
RELEASE-001: full acceptance journey, deployment, host, chain, and accessibility evidence
knownBlockers: PR #10 settlement routes still require payer/receiver authorization and fully atomic pay/confirm/close transitions.
Frontend money models still expose decimal JavaScript numbers and must be migrated in DATA-002.
The completion branch is not directly mergeable because it removes authoritative backend, CI, deployment, and security infrastructure.
The completion branch verification currently fails TypeScript checks and has no valid QUALITY-002 merge or PR #11 in the repository.
Legacy Cypress, browser-smoke, edge-function, and full-release runtimes are absent from the mvp source and remain capability-gated until deliberately reconciled.
